mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of future earnings for equities and thus producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
regime_hint: tightening phase of the Fed policy cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the identified tightening episode, with p-value > 0.05 in a two-tailed test against the pre-tightening period.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the same month
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, returns are negative or statistically indistinguishable from zero (p > 0.05) despite the labor signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 2% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating economic demand, which elevates corporate earnings expectations and produces positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly growth > 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant return advantage in the 20-day window (p > 0.05) even when INDPRO is above threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer inflation measured by CPIAUCSL (monthly CPI YoY) falling below 3% signals supply-side easing, lowering growth expectations and generating negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 3% in a month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% over 6 months indicate labor market resilience, prompting the Fed to hold rates steady longer, which supports equity valuations and yields positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or not statistically different from baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in labor turnover (PAYEMS) accompanied by a rise in hourly wage growth (not directly observable here, but implied by labor strength) reduces turnover costs and boosts productivity, leading to positive S&P 500 60-day returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls by >10% from previous month
failure_condition: No significant return improvement over 60 days despite the labor signal (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the 10-year yield proxy (implied by FEDFUNDS path) above 4% suggests higher real rates, which compresses discounting of future equities and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months indicates persistent supply-side weakness, lowering growth forecasts and resulting in negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or the signal is not predictive (p > 0.05).
